product.reading: Reading requests and who has access now.

statusDetail.pending: Waiting for someone other than the requester to approve it.
statusDetail.ended: Ended: its time ran out, or the requester was done. Its certificates no longer work.
statusDetail.revoked: Revoked before its time. Its certificates are on the revocation list.

requestsPage.description_one: Access to {{count}} server only when someone asks and someone else approves. It ends by itself.
requestsPage.description_other: Access to {{count}} servers only when someone asks and someone else approves. It ends by itself.
requestsPage.needFactor: Add a second factor to ask for or approve access
requestsPage.needFactorDetail: Asking for access, approving it and getting a certificate need a sign-in with a second factor. Add an authenticator app or a passkey under Account, then sign in again with it. Signing in through your identity provider counts.
requestsPage.waitingEditor: Approve or deny what others asked for. You can never approve your own.
requestsPage.waitingViewer: Editors approve; nobody approves their own.
requestsPage.noneWaitingDetail: When someone asks for access, it shows here for the others to decide.
requestsPage.askDetail: For yourself, for as long as you need and no longer.
requestsPage.reasonPlaceholder: What you will do, and why it cannot wait
requestsPage.ticketHint: Optional: the incident or change, such as INC-2291.
requestsPage.needsOne: Someone other than you must approve it.
requestsPage.needsTwo: Two people other than you must approve it.
requestsPage.noneMine: You have not asked for access yet
requestsPage.perDayDetail: Asked for, and granted, over the last 14 days.

welcomePage.description: Nobody keeps a key to your servers. People ask for access when they need it, someone else approves, and the certificate they get stops working when the access ends.
welcomePage.step1: Add a server, with the accounts people may ask for and how long.
welcomePage.step2: Run its setup once on the server: it trusts Access for those accounts, on that server only.
welcomePage.step3: Invite the people who ask as viewers and the team leads who approve as editors.
welcomePage.step4: Remove the keys in authorized_keys. Until then, nothing has changed.
welcomePage.askAdmin: An admin of Access adds the servers.

requestPage.openFor: Open for {{left}} more. Get a certificate below and log in.
requestPage.getCertificateDetail: For your own SSH key. It works on this server only, as this account, until the access ends.
requestPage.publicKeyHint: The .pub file, such as ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub. Your private key never leaves your computer.
requestPage.save: Save it next to your key, with -cert.pub after its name. ssh finds it there on its own.
requestPage.notFoundDetail: It may be in another Access.

openPage.description: Who can log in where right now, and for how much longer.
openPage.noneDetail: That is how it should be most of the time.
openPage.sessions: A session already open is not closed when access ends
openPage.sessionsDetail: The certificate stops new logins at its end, and a revoked one within a minute, when the server fetches the revocation list. Closing sessions that are already open needs the session proxy, which is not built yet.

historyPage.description: Every request, newest first, and what became of it.

serversPage.description: The servers people may ask for, and the policy of each: which accounts, how long and how many approvals.
serversPage.name: Name
serversPage.nameHint: Part of every certificate's principal, such as deploy@api-prod-03.
serversPage.loginsHint: The Unix accounts one may ask to log in as, separated by commas. They must exist on the server.
serversPage.descriptionPlaceholder: Optional, such as Orders API, production
serversPage.noneDetail: An admin adds the servers people may ask for.

auditPage.description: Every request, approval, certificate, change and sign-in, and every attempt that was refused. Nothing here can be changed or removed.

setupPage.description: How a server comes to trust Access, and how people log in with it.
setupPage.caDetail: Servers trust this public key. Its private key never leaves Access. Fingerprint {{fingerprint}}.
setupPage.serverDetail: Run once as root. They trust the CA for the server's own accounts only, and fetch the revocation list every minute.
setupPage.peopleDetail: Nothing to install: OpenSSH has done certificates since 2010.
setupPage.people1: Ask for access on Requests, with a reason and how long.
setupPage.people2: Once someone else approves, paste your public key on the request and save the certificate next to your key.
setupPage.people3: Connect with ssh as usual. When the access ends, the certificate stops working; ask again next time.

settingsPage.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this Access.

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this Access, and with which role. Viewers see everything and ask for access for themselves; editors also approve and revoke what others asked for; admins also keep the servers, and manage members and tokens.

signin.title: Sign-in
signin.description: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: For scripts and a SIEM. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once. A token can never ask for, approve or use access.
